data.title: Spain Inflation Eases To 4-month Low
data.description:
MADRID (dpa-AFX) - Spain's consumer price inflation eased more-than-expected in November to the lowest level in four months, flash data from the statistical office INE revealed Friday.

The consumer price index climbed 4.1 percent annually in November, slower than October's stable increase of 4.9 percent. Economists had expected inflation to moderate to 4.6 percent. Core inflation also eased to 2.6 percent from 3.1 percent in October.

The slowdown in inflation was mainly due to the fall in the prices of fuel and lubricants for private vehicles.

Similarly, inflation based on the harmonized index of consumer prices softened to 4.1 percent from 4.9 percent.

On a monthly basis, consumer prices dropped 0.6 percent, reversing a 0.6 percent increase in October. Moreover, this was the first decline in ten months.

Separate official data showed that retail sales decreased 1.0 percent annually in October, slower than the 1.4 percent contraction in September. It was the third successive drop in a row. Monthly, sales rebounded 0.3 percent versus a 0.3 percent fall in the prior month.

data.title: Chile's antitrust authority seeks $80 million Apple fine over iOS
data.description:
Chile's competition authority (FNE) asked the country's antitrust court on Friday to fine Apple about $80 million and order corrective measures for abusing its dominant position in the iOS operating system market.

  • The regulator said the US technology firm has restricted competition in app distribution and in-app payments for digital goods on iOS since at least 2019

  • The fine sought is equivalent to 30% of sales from the product lines and services linked to the infringement during the period investigated, the FNE said on X

  • "The FNE verified that Apple has prevented the sideloading of applications and alternative app stores from web browsers on iPhone devices, forcing developers and consumers to rely exclusively on the App Store," it said

  • Apple argued the restrictions were necessary for security and privacy reasons, but the regulator found the measures were unnecessary and disproportionate

  • The FNE wants the antitrust court to require Apple to allow third-party apps and app stores, alternative in-app billing, and payment buttons that send users to external payment systems without friction

data.title: SpaceX Stock Rises. Elon Musk Makes Billion-Dollar Pledge to American Children
data.description:
SpaceX shares climbed about 5% in premarket trading after Elon Musk committed to matching the company's planned contribution to investment accounts for eligible American children.

Musk's commitment could bring the combined contribution to approximately $18.4 billion, based on an estimated 72 million U.S. children and SpaceX's current share price. The final value will depend on the number of eligible recipients and the terms of the distribution.

SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell has separately pledged more than two million shares. Neither executive disclosed how the shares would be allocated or when recipients could receive them.

The Trump Accounts program provides eligible children born between 2025 and 2028 with an initial $1,000 contribution from the U.S. Treasury. Families, friends and employers can add up to $5,000 annually, with funds invested in a qualifying low-cost index fund for long-term growth.

The initiative has also attracted contributions from major technology companies, including Micron Technology (MU), Intel (INTC), Broadcom (AVGO) and IBM . CNBC reported that donations from individuals and families have exceeded $1 billion, adding to corporate participation in the program.

data.title: Adani Group to list airport business in FY28; plans $140 billion capex over five years
data.description:
The Adani Group will prepare the ground for a potential listing of its airport business, with the corporate structure expected to be ready next year, paving the way for a possible demerger or initial public offering in FY28.

Jugeshinder (Robbie) Singh, Group CFO, Adani Group, said the group is working to ensure the airport business can fund its own investment programme and that its revenue profile is aligned with the proposed structure. The share of non-aeronautical revenue in the airport business is currently about 60 per cent, and the group expects it to rise to 65 per cent or more over time, he said on the sidelines of the India Debt Capital Market Summit organised by the Trust Group on Friday.

Non-aeronautical revenue includes income from retail, food and beverages, advertising, commercial property, and other passenger-related services, and it is an important component of an airport's profitability.

‘Significant potential’

On a possible venture into the aviation sector, he said the group would rather remain an investor and let an entrepreneur run the business. The group believes India’s aviation infrastructure has significant growth potential, he said, pointing out that the country currently has about 3,200-3,300 flights a day against a potential of 30,000 as air travel penetration increases.

Given the potential demand, the group has requested that the government allow it to fund a company seeking to venture directly into aviation, said Singh.

Focus on domestic funding

Adani Power is expected to emerge as a large issuer in the domestic public and private debt markets. Other group companies are also looking to tap domestic capital markets through equity and debt issuances, said Singh.

The group plans to continue its annual equity-raising programme of about $2-4 billion, primarily to broaden its shareholder base and bring in more long-term investors rather than meet immediate funding requirements.

Adani Power and Adani Energy Solutions are also exploring qualified institutional placements (QIPs), largely to improve their shareholder registers.

The group is considering issuing long-dated dollar bonds after April, potentially with a 20-year maturity. While around $600 million of debt is approaching maturity, the relevant businesses have sufficient cash to retire it. The proposed issuance would partly help extend the maturity profile of borrowings, he added.

The Adani Group plans to invest around $140 billion over the next five years across its infrastructure and energy businesses. “We would like our capital markets and domestic markets to account for about 70-75 per cent of total capital markets, like Australia and Japan,” he said.

In the longer term, the domestic share could increase to 75-80 per cent, with global funding accounting for the balance. The group expects to repay around $25-30 billion of bank borrowings over the next five to 10 years, while continuing to raise fresh funds to finance expansion.

Data-centre funding

On data-centre financing, the group said it had secured an overall funding arrangement of about $3 billion for its AdaniConnex business, of which about $900 million has been drawn down. The facility is expected to be drawn in tranches of $1.6 billion and $1.4 billion. The funding requirement could increase to around $10 billion over the next four years as the business expands.

The group is initially relying on external commercial borrowings (ECBs) to finance its data centre and digital connectivity businesses, as this is currently the easiest route to funding.

data.title: SKINN launches Signatures fragrance line with Silk Rose, Sea Breeze
data.description:
SKINN, the fine fragrance brand of Titan Company Limited, has launched Signatures, a two-fragrance collection comprising Silk Rose for women and Sea Breeze for men. The collection is priced at ₹4,495 for 100ml.

The launch took place at The St. Regis, Mumbai. Attendees included actor and SKINN brand ambassador Shobhita Dhulipala, Manish Gupta, CEO of Titan’s Fragrances and Accessories Division, and perfumers Nanako Ogi and Hamid Merati-Kashani, who created the two fragrances.

Two fragrances inspired by floral and marine notes

Silk Rose is a floral-fruity Eau de Parfum inspired by Turkish roses, with notes including lemon, raspberry, peony, jasmine and white musk. Sea Breeze is a woody-marine fragrance featuring bergamot, grapefruit, pink pepper, sandalwood and marine accords. Dhulipala and Ayushmann Khurrana, also a SKINN ambassador, feature in the respective product films.

Signatures will be sold at Titan World stores, SKINN kiosks, Shoppers Stop and Lifestyle, and on skinn.in. SKINN currently operates 18 kiosks in India.

SKINN reported 28 per cent year-on-year growth and expects to sustain growth of 20–25 per cent. It has about 5,000 distribution doors across more than 300 towns. E-commerce accounts for roughly 50 per cent of sales, retail 30 per cent and general trade 20 per cent. The brand aims to reach 8 million customers by FY30.

India’s fragrance market offers growth opportunities

The company said India’s fragrance market grew about 15 per cent in 2025, while formal fragrance penetration stands at an estimated 8–10 per cent. Men make up about 55 per cent of SKINN’s customers and women 45 per cent, compared with a 70:30 split in the traditional mass fragrance category.

“As consumers become increasingly discerning in their fragrance choices, we see a significant opportunity to elevate their experience,” Gupta said, adding that Signatures reflects the company’s ambition to strengthen its premium portfolio.

Launched in 2013, SKINN works with international perfumers and fragrance houses. Titan Company shares closed at ₹4,675.30 on the NSE on 27 November, up 0.95 per cent.

data.title: Ecommerce, BNPL Stocks Outpace Brick-and-Mortar Peers as Black Friday Kicks Off
data.description:
By Adriano Marchese

Digital shopping platforms and buy-now-pay-later providers rallied premarket, while North American big-box and mall retailers barely budged amid household budget pressures and tariff headwinds.

Ecommerce platforms and digital installment lenders climbed in premarket trading Friday, outpacing traditional brick-and-mortar retailers as bargain-hunting shoppers turn online for Black Friday amid broader trends of inflation, tariffs and stretched household budgets.

Online commerce bellwethers led the early gains, with Shopify rising 4.5%, Etsy gaining 2% and Wayfair adding 1.7%. Buy-now-pay-later providers also advanced, paced by Affirm, up 4.1%, and Sezzle up 3.2%

By contrast, mass-market and off-price chains were muted to lower. Burlington Stores slipped 0.4% and Gap fell 0.7%, while Walmart, Costco Wholesale and Target were little changed.

The early gains in online shopping and installment-payment shares tracked a broader premarket rebound across U.S. stock indexes led by artificial-intelligence names, with Nasdaq futures up 2% and S&P 500 and Dow futures rising 1.4% and 1.2%, respectively.

Retail chains with heavy overseas merchandise exposure face renewed trade uncertainty after President Donald Trump this week proposed new tariffs on over a dozen trading partners, including China, the EU and Japan, citing excess industrial capacity.

In the run up to the holiday season, the National Retail Federation projects U.S. holiday sales across November and December to rise 4.2% to $1.013 trillion over 2025 levels, with nearly 183 million consumers expected to shop during the Thanksgiving weekend this year.

Despite the rosier expectations for spending in the latter part of the year, many of the digital commerce and installment-payment names entered Friday down between 17% and 19% for the year, compared with defensive staples like Walmart and Costco, which are up 18% and 26% year to date.

U.S. stock exchanges were closed Thursday and will close early at 1 p.m. ET on Friday.

data.title: BAE Systems Secures $6 Billion in Combat-Vehicle Contracts For Several European Nations
data.description:
By Mauro Orru

BAE Systems said it had secured $6 billion in contracts to supply hundreds of combat vehicles to several European nations as they seek to buttress their armed forces amid high geopolitical tensions.

The U.K. arms maker said it would provide more than 400 CV90 combat vehicles to the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden, Finland and Lithuania under contracts awarded through separate purchase-order agreements.

The group said support systems, training, spare parts, special tools and test equipment were part of the deal and that the vehicles and components would be produced through a distributed supplier network across those nations.

data.title: AI math breakthroughs revive Bitcoin security fears, but practical threat remains unproven: K33
data.description:
AI's progress in mathematics warrants closer attention to Bitcoin's cryptographic security, but recent mathematical breakthroughs have not demonstrated a compromise of its cryptography, analysts at research and brokerage firm K33 said Friday.

Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge last week announced a proposed proof of the Riemann hypothesis, a conjecture dating to 1859 about the distribution of prime numbers. He worked on the problem using Claude. Independent researchers have checked the proof computationally, with academic review still ongoing.

"Naturally, this has reignited fears surrounding the mathematical assumptions underpinning Bitcoin and modern cryptography," the analysts wrote, though the Riemann proof does not itself provide a way to attack cryptography.

Another recent debate in the crypto industry focused on P versus NP, with implications extending to modern banking systems, secure internet communications, and digital signatures.

Bitcoin's (BTC) transaction signatures rely on how difficult it is to derive a private key from a public key, while the reverse is relatively easy, K33 said. To explain P versus NP, the analysts described the analogy of a large Sudoku puzzle. Verifying the answer is relatively easy, whereas finding the solution itself is substantially more demanding, they said.

"In simple terms, P represents problems that can be solved efficiently, while NP represents problems for which a proposed solution can be verified efficiently," the analysts said. If P equals NP, an algorithm must exist to solve even arbitrarily large Sudoku puzzles in polynomial time, meaning that the computational effort grows at a mathematically manageable rate as the puzzle grows, they said.

Mathematical and practical limits

For Bitcoin, proving P equals NP would mean an algorithm must theoretically exist to derive private keys in polynomial time, K33 said. The analysts cited computer scientist Donald Knuth, who has long argued that P may equal NP but that proving it might not be of much use. A proof would not necessarily tell anyone how to build the algorithm, they said, and even if it could, it might still take too long to run.

However, proving P does not equal NP, the prevailing belief among computer scientists, would not guarantee Bitcoin's security either, as faster algorithms targeting its particular cryptography could still emerge, the analysts said.

"For now, P versus NP remains unsolved, and recent mathematical breakthroughs do not establish that Bitcoin's cryptography has been compromised," they said.

Earlier this week, Zcash infrastructure team Zakura urged users to migrate away from its legacy Sapling shielded pool, citing the Riemann claim and unsubstantiated rumors of advances in integer factorization. "Practical pairing breaks are highly speculative," Zakura said. Neither factoring nor pairings is used by the Ironwood shielded pool or transparent transactions, according to the team.

Meanwhile, the Ethereum Foundation recently doubled its protocol security team, saying AI was a "more urgent risk" than quantum computing, with models finding software vulnerabilities and beginning to improve on decades-old algorithms. However, that did not mean AI can or will break the assumptions that cryptography relies on, the foundation said. It is working toward a 2029 internal deadline to introduce alternative hash-based cryptography for validators, user accounts, and data blobs.

data.title: U.S. Natural Gas Futures Fall As Front Month Shifts to January — Market Talk
data.description: U.S. natural gas futures are lower as the Nymex January contract debuts at the front of the curve with the market anticipating a relatively mild winter. Storage data on Wednesday showed the first withdrawal of the season, with inventories standing 80 Bcf above the five-year average. "Inventories remain in healthy territory relative to historical benchmarks, leaving the market well positioned heading into the peak heating season," Andy Huenefeld of Pinebrook Energy Advisors said in a note. Natural gas for January delivery is down 4.7% at $3.485/mmBtu. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)

data.title: Lifco acquires EG Medical in Italy
data.description:
Lifco has signed an agreement to acquire all shares in the Italian company EG Medical S.r.l. EG Medical is a niche manufacturer of trays for surgical instruments.

In 2025, EG Medical reported net sales of approximately EUR 11.9 million. The company is based in Villafranca Padovana in Padua, Italy and has 32 employees. EG Medical will be consolidated in Business Area Dental. Consolidation is expected to take place in the fourth quarter of 2026.

The acquisition will not have any significant effect on Lifco’s earnings or financial position in the 2026 financial year.
